title: A fibre nonzerodivisor cuts a flat hypersurface near the point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], let $x\in X$ with $s=f(x)$, and suppose $f$ is flat at $x$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $h\in\mathfrak m_x\subset\mathcal O_{X,x}$ be a germ whose image $\bar h$ in $\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is a nonzerodivisor (multiplication by $\bar h$ is injective), where $X_s$ is the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There exist an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ of $x$ and $a\in B$ with germ $h$ such that the closed subscheme $D=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(a))\hookrightarrow U$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] contains $x$, and the composite $D\to U\to X\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 056Y, label lemma-slice-given-element; forget the additional assertion that D is an effective Cartier divisor.

proof.text: Choose affine neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $s$ and $U_1=\operatorname{Spec}B_1$ of $x$, with $f(U_1)\subseteq V$ and $B_1$ finitely presented over $A$, by the definition of local finite presentation. Write $\mathfrak q_1$ for $x$ and $\mathfrak p$ for $s$. The affine-stalk localization statement writes the specified germ as $h=b/t$ in $(B_1)_{\mathfrak q_1}$, with $t\notin\mathfrak q_1$. Replace $U_1$ by its affine principal open $D(t)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_1)_t$ and let $a=b/t$ be its section. It has germ exactly $h$. Finite presentation is preserved here directly: if $B_1=A[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)$ and $t$ is represented by $T$, then $(B_1)_t=A[T_1,\ldots,T_n,u]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m,uT-1)$. Rename this ring $B$, and the point prime $\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: first paragraph, affine restriction and extension of the germ to a section; explicit principal-localization presentation

proof.text: The stalk maps identify flatness at $x$ with flatness of $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak q}$. By flatness over a localization, $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is also flat over $A$. Apply openness of flatness to the finitely presented $A$-algebra $B$ and the free rank-one $B$-module $M=B$. Choose a basic open $D(g)$ containing $\mathfrak q$ in that open locus. For every $\mathfrak r\in D(g)$, $B_{\mathfrak r}$ is flat over $A$, hence over $A_{\mathfrak r\cap A}$ by flatness over a localization. The affine-stalk identifications and the definition of flatness therefore show that $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat. Its full affine chart in the affine criterion gives that $B_g$ is flat as an $A$-module. Replace $B$ by $B_g$ and $a$ by its restriction, retaining its germ and finite presentation by the same extra-variable presentation as in Step 1. Thus from now on $A\to B$ is flat and finitely presented, not merely flat at the specified point.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: first paragraph, openness of flatness; algebraic form is Tag 00RC and localization is Tag 00HT (2)

proof.text: Apply the flat finite-presentation model theorem to $A\to B$. It supplies a finitely presented $\mathbf Z$-algebra $P$, a flat finitely presented $P$-algebra $Q$, a map $P\to A$, and an $A$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_P Q\cong B$. Use this isomorphism to regard the chosen section $a$ as an element of this tensor product. This is the flat Noetherian-approximation input of 056Y, in its algebraic version (02JO), before ensuring that the one chosen section descends.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: second paragraph, Algebra Tag 02JO (1), with the module equal to the algebra

proof.text: Write $a=\sum_{j=1}^N a_j\otimes q_j$ with $a_j\in A$ and $q_j\in Q$. Let $A_0\subseteq A$ be the $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by the images of a finite generating set of $P$ together with the finitely many $a_j$. The map $P\to A$ factors through $A_0$. Put $B_0=A_0\otimes_P Q$ and $a_0=\sum_j a_j\otimes q_j\in B_0$. Flat base change and finite-presentation base change give that $A_0\to B_0$ is flat and finitely presented. The maps $a'\otimes(a_0'\otimes q')\mapsto a'a_0'\otimes q'$ and $a'\otimes q'\mapsto a'\otimes(1\otimes q')$ are inverse $A$-algebra isomorphisms $A\otimes_{A_0}B_0\cong A\otimes_P Q=B$, and send $1\otimes a_0$ to $a$. Thus the section as well as the morphism has descended; no finite generation assumption on $A$ was used.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: second paragraph, descending the section after the flat model; the finite coefficient enlargement is written out

proof.text: Every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is generated by its least positive element, or is zero, so $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian. The ring $A_0$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ by its displayed finite generating set. The finite-type-algebra Noetherian theorem gives that $A_0$ is Noetherian. Since $B_0$ is finitely presented, hence of finite type, over $A_0$, the same theorem gives that $B_0$ is Noetherian. These are assertions about the model only, not about $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: second paragraph, the affine Noetherian base and model; Algebra Tag 00FN

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q_0=\mathfrak q\cap B_0$, $\mathfrak p_0=\mathfrak p\cap A_0$, $k_0=\kappa(\mathfrak p_0)$ and $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The map $A_0\to A$ induces a field embedding $k_0\to k$: first localize at the two primes, then pass to their residue fields. Put $E_0=B_0\otimes_{A_0}k_0$. The definition of the fibre and the affine fibre-product theorem identify the model fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}E_0$. They identify the original fibre chart with $\operatorname{Spec}E$, where $E=B\otimes_A k\cong E_0\otimes_{k_0}k$; the isomorphism sends $(b_0\otimes c)\otimes d$ to $b_0\otimes cd$ in $B_0\otimes_{A_0}k$, with inverse $b_0\otimes d\mapsto(b_0\otimes1)\otimes d$. Let $\mathfrak r$ be the prime of $E$ at $x$ and $\mathfrak r_0$ its contraction to $E_0$, the fibre point at $\mathfrak q_0$. The affine-stalk theorem gives $C=E_{\mathfrak r}=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ and $C_0=(E_0)_{\mathfrak r_0}$. The fibre-stalk quotient theorem also gives $C_0\cong (B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}/\mathfrak p_0(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$, preserving the images of $a_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: second paragraph, the displayed cartesian model and the two local rings on its fibres; Schemes Tags 01I4, 01JQ and 0HA1

proof.text: The field-extension base-change theorem makes $E_0\to E_0\otimes_{k_0}k=E$ faithfully flat, hence flat. Localizing at $\mathfrak r$ and its contraction $\mathfrak r_0$ gives a flat local homomorphism $C_0\to C$ by the flat-local-ring-maps theorem. A flat local homomorphism is faithfully flat. The universal-injectivity theorem, applied with module $N=C_0$ and $C_0\otimes_{C_0}C\cong C$, therefore makes this map injective. If $a_0z=0$ in $C_0$, its image in $C$ is killed by the specified fibre element $\bar h$, which is a nonzerodivisor by hypothesis. Its image is zero, hence $z=0$. Thus $\bar a_0$ is a nonzerodivisor in $C_0$. Moreover $a_0\in\mathfrak q_0$, since its germ $h$ lies in the maximal ideal at $x$; consequently $\bar a_0$ lies in the maximal ideal of $C_0$. The quotient $C_0/(\bar a_0)$ is nonzero, as that ideal is proper. By the regular-sequence definition the singleton $(\bar a_0)$ is therefore a regular sequence in $C_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: second paragraph, faithful flatness of the map of fibre local rings and descent of the nonzerodivisor

proof.text: Apply the flat-local-ring-maps theorem to the flat map $A_0\to B_0$. By Step 5 its localized map $(A_0)_{\mathfrak p_0}\to(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}$ is a flat local homomorphism between Noetherian local rings. Its closed fibre is precisely the quotient identified with $C_0$ in Step 6. Step 7 verifies the regular-sequence hypothesis of the Grothendieck regular-sequence flatness theorem for $c=1$ and $f_1=a_0/1$. That theorem gives $(B_0)_{\mathfrak q_0}/(a_0)$ flat over $(A_0)_{\mathfrak p_0}$. Flatness over a localization then makes this quotient flat over $A_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: last paragraph, the application of Algebra Tag 00MF, equivalently the singleton case of 00MG

proof.text: Set $M=B_0/(a_0)$. This is a finitely presented $B_0$-module, presented by $B_0\xrightarrow{a_0}B_0\to M\to0$, and $A_0\to B_0$ is finitely presented. Step 8 says $M_{\mathfrak q_0}$ is flat over $A_0$. Apply openness of flatness to obtain a basic open $D(g_0)$ containing $\mathfrak q_0$ on which every $M_{\mathfrak r}$ is flat over $A_0$. Put $H_0=(B_0)_{g_0}/(a_0)$. For a prime of $H_0$, let $\mathfrak r\subset B_0$ be its inverse image; then $g_0\notin\mathfrak r$ and $a_0\in\mathfrak r$. Its local ring is $M_{\mathfrak r}=(B_0)_{\mathfrak r}/(a_0)$: the identification sends $(b/g_0^n)/d$ to the same fraction in the quotient of $(B_0)_{\mathfrak r}$, with inverse induced by $b/t\mapsto(b/1)/(t/1)$. It is flat over $A_0$, and over $(A_0)_{\mathfrak r\cap A_0}$ by flatness over a localization. Affine-stalk identification and the definition of flatness show that $\operatorname{Spec}H_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ is flat. The affine criterion on its full affine chart now says $H_0$ is flat over $A_0$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: last paragraph, spreading flatness of the quotient by Algebra Tag 00RC; only the flat-quotient part of the claim is required

proof.text: Let $g\in B=A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$ be the image of $g_0$, which is not in $\mathfrak q$ since $g_0\notin\mathfrak q_0$. The affine principal open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ is therefore a neighbourhood of $x$ inside the original $X$. Restrict the section $a$ to $B_g$. There is an $A$-algebra isomorphism $A\otimes_{A_0}H_0\cong B_g/(a)$, given by $c\otimes\overline{b/g_0^n}\mapsto\overline{c\,b/g^n}$. Its inverse is induced from $A\to A\otimes H_0$, $c\mapsto c\otimes1$, and $B_0\to A\otimes H_0$, $b\mapsto1\otimes\bar b$; $g_0$ is a unit and $a_0$ is zero there, so it factors through localization and quotient. The two maps are inverse on the ring generators. Since $H_0$ is flat over $A_0$, flat base change makes $H=B_g/(a)$ flat over $A$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: second paragraph, returning the quotient to the original base; direct base change of the flat quotient suffices because the Cartier assertion is not part of this item

proof.text: Put $D=\operatorname{Spec}H$. For every prime $\mathfrak t$ of $H$ with inverse image $\mathfrak v$ in $A$, flatness of $A\to H$ gives the flat local homomorphism $A_{\mathfrak v}\to H_{\mathfrak t}$. These are exactly the stalk maps of $D\to V\subseteq S$ by affine-stalk localization. The stalks of the affine open $V$ equal the stalks of $S$ at its points, so these are also the stalk maps of the required composite $D\to U\to X\to S$. The definition of flatness proves that this composite is flat at every point of $D$.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: conclusion, flatness of the base-changed hypersurface over the original scheme

proof.text: Finally write the current $B$ as $A[T_1,\ldots,T_n]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m)$, and choose polynomials $G,H_a$ representing $g,a$. Then $H=B_g/(a)\cong A[T_1,\ldots,T_n,u]/(F_1,\ldots,F_m,uG-1,H_a)$. This finite presentation and the affine neighbourhood $V\subseteq S$ witness local finite presentation at every point of $D$, by its definition. The surjection $B_g\to H$ makes $D\hookrightarrow U$ a closed immersion by the affine quotient description of closed immersions. The restricted section still has germ $h$. Since $h\in\mathfrak m_x$, its representing $a$ lies in the prime of $x$ in $B_g$ (the inverse image of the maximal ideal under the prime localization map). Thus $x\in V(a)=D$. Rename the ring $B_g$ as the $B$ in the statement; this is the required affine neighbourhood, section and closed subscheme.

source.place: Tag 056Y, lemma-slice-given-element, proof: conclusion, local finite presentation, the prescribed germ and containment of the point
